learning_outcomes.text: Analyze environmental problems by applying state-of-the-art technologies specifically applied to the industrial sector.
Identify and classify all types of waste generated by human activity.
Visualize the environmental impacts produced in all industrial sectors under an integrated approach.
Analyze, characterize, manage, minimize, and treat both industrial wastewater and hazardous waste.
Know the applicable legislation for each type of waste, particularly hazardous waste.

Present a report detailing, for a given industrial sector and its geographical location: suitability of the installation to the legal framework, description of treatments for hazardous waste management, available technologies, and description of internal management measures for minimizing hazardous waste and improving its management.
Know the architecture of internal combustion engines and their thermodynamic cycles.
Know the methods of engine testing and their application in the laboratory to perform experimental analyses to evaluate state variables and characteristic curves.
Be able to work in a team, apply critical reasoning, make decisions, and communicate knowledge and conclusions in the field of industrial engineering.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1: Environmental Management in the Company
Topic 2: Waste: classifications, legal framework, and management.
Topic 3: Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) and its management.
Topic 4: Toxic and Hazardous Waste. Waste minimization
assessment_rules: To release content from partial tests (PP1a, PP2a, PP1b, PP2b), a minimum score of 4 points is required on each. If a partial test score is below 4 points, the student must take an exam on that content in the ordinary call, retaining seminar grades. To pass the ordinary call exam, a minimum of 3 points must be obtained in each partial exam taken. In the extraordinary call, previously approved or compensated parts are not retained; only seminar grades are kept in the same proportion as the ordinary call. If no seminars were completed, the exam score accounts for 100% of the course.
